title: STRIDE Threat Model Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Software Architecture
description: Apply STRIDE to a data flow diagram of a healthcare patient portal: select any component or data flow, read the threat in each applicable category, and record a mitigation for it while a tracker shows which of the six categories you have covered.

educational.topic: Threat modeling with STRIDE on a data flow diagram
learningObjectives: Students will be able to apply the STRIDE framework to a system's data flow diagram, identifying at least one threat from each STRIDE category for the depicted system.
prerequisites: Data flow diagrams and trust boundaries

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked application of a framework to a concrete system, with commit-then-reveal mitigations and coverage feedback
keyQuestions: Which STRIDE categories apply to this kind of element, and which do not?
Which security property does each threat violate?
Which data flows cross a trust boundary, and what changes at the boundary?
commonMisconceptions: Every STRIDE category applies to every element (a data flow has no identity to spoof and no privileges to elevate).
Traffic inside the trusted zone needs no protection (internal flows still face tampering and disclosure).
A threat model is finished once each category has one threat (coverage of categories is a minimum, not completeness).
assessmentOpportunities: Give students a new element (for example, an appointment-reminder service that sends SMS messages) and ask for one threat per applicable STRIDE category with a mitigation each, plus one security scenario written in six-part form.
